source.title_on_document: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Collaborative Ideation: Educational Insight from Fashion Students

paper_design_summary: Ten fashion students were selected, five per group, for a design workshop of three 40-minute sessions (mood map, style map, sketch); Group A worked without image-generative AI and Group B used Midjourney, with allocation method unstated (pp. 3-4, Sections III.B-C). Three experts rated the creations on 7-point scales using CAT and CPAM criteria, and semi-structured interviews were also reported; the selected sample is not a separately confirmed analysis N (p. 4, Sections III.C-D; p. 14, Table III).

studies.label: Fashion ideation design workshop (Group A no AI vs Group B Midjourney)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Use of the image-generative AI platform Midjourney (Group B) or no AI platform (Group A) during the workshop; method of allocation to groups is not described
assignment.quote: The workshop participants were divided into two groups: Group A did not use an image-generative AI platform, while Group B used an image-generative AI platform, Midjourney.

arms.name: Group B
arms.description: Five selected workshop participants (p. 4, Section III.C); analysis N unreported. Used Midjourney plus basic graphic tools (Photoshop, Illustrator) and pencil/paper; received an extra 20-minute explanation of the platform (pp. 3-4, Section III.B).

arms.name: Group A
arms.description: Five selected workshop participants (p. 4, Section III.C); analysis N unreported. No image-generative AI platform; basic graphic tools (Photoshop, Illustrator) and pencil/paper (pp. 3-4, Section III.B).

participants.exclusions: No exclusions or analysis flow are reported. Ten people (five per group) were selected as research participants (p. 4, Section III.C); Table III does not state how many people or creations contributed to each analysis (p. 14).
participants.who: College students majoring in fashion in their third to fourth year who aspired to become fashion designers; recruited by purposive snowball sampling; seven women and three men, aged 22-26
participants.quote: a total of ten people (five for each group) were selected as research participants, using purposive snowball sampling methods. The participants were college students who aspired to become fashion designers
participants.locator: p. 4, Section III.C Participants and Interviews

ai_tool.how_used: Group B generated images from text prompts (and reference images) for mood maps, style maps, and sketch references

task.description: Fashion ideation on the theme 'fun': Session 1 mind map and mood map, Session 2 fashion style map (collage), Session 3 sketch
task.duration: Three sessions of 40 minutes each, 120 minutes in total; Group B also received an additional 20-minute explanation of Midjourney

outcomes.name: Originality of Session 1 mood map (expert rating, CAT criteria)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: CAT criterion for the Session 1 mood map: Expert-rated originality. Three fashion-design experts with doctoral degrees and more than three years of teaching experience rated creations on a 7-point Likert scale (p. 4, Section III.D). The paper does not specify whether expert ratings were averaged within creations or pooled, or how multiple creations per person were handled. The analysis unit, analysis N and n_units therefore remain unconfirmed; the arm SDs cannot be treated as confirmed participant-level SDs (p. 14, Table III). Midjourney was available to Group B during this workshop session (pp. 3-4, Section III.B; pp. 6-7, Section IV.B.2).

eligibility.reason: Ten people were selected, five per group (p. 4, Section III.C), so the reported workshop pool is below 50 people even though the analyzed N is not separately reported (p. 14, Table III). The paper compares Group A without image-generative AI and Group B with Midjourney but does not report the allocation method (pp. 3-4, Section III.B), leaving random assignment unclear. Experts scored participants' creations (p. 4, Section III.D; p. 14, Table III), meeting the output criterion. Retain quasi_people provisionally and map it to observational context under the form-spec design_class note and codebook Section 3; core eligibility remains no.

one_line_finding: In a workshop with ten selected students, five per group (p. 4, Section III.C), Group B had higher expert-rated originality averages in all three sessions, including sketch originality 5.4 vs 3.9 and newness 5.1 vs 3.7 on a 7-point scale, with no inferential tests reported (p. 4, Section III.D; p. 14, Table III).
open_questions: How many participants and creations contributed to each Table III analysis, and were expert ratings averaged within creations or pooled as separate ratings? The paper does not state analysis Ns or the unit underlying the averages and SDs (p. 4, Section III.D; p. 14, Table III).

Did Group B retain access to Midjourney during sketching? Earlier AI-generated images are confirmed as assistance, but continued platform access or explicit withdrawal is not stated (pp. 7-8, Section IV.B.2, S3; p. 8, Section IV.C).
notes: The 15-outcome limit is filled with the three originality scores, separate newness scores for Sessions 2 and 3, the remaining Session 1 CAT criteria, and solvency, sophistication and usefulness for Sessions 2 and 3. No outcome is explicitly designated primary. Attractiveness (AC) for Sessions 2 and 3 is omitted from the outcome list under the limit, prioritizing novelty, appropriateness/usefulness, detail and source-use criteria (p. 14, Table III and abbreviations; form-spec rule 7). Completeness is named for Sessions 2 and 3 in the methods but has no separate Table III column, so no completeness statistics are entered (p. 4, Section III.D; p. 14, Table III). Diversity of source use concerns an individual creation and is not across-person diversity. Table II contains qualitative creative-process comparisons, not additional numerical output scores (p. 13). All entered Table III avr and sd entries, including the A-B rows, are reproduced as printed without recalculation; entries labeled A-B sd are not reported standard errors and include negative values. Only descriptive arm averages/SDs and A-B rows are available; analysis Ns, aggregation details and inferential statistics are absent. Direction records the ordering of printed arm averages, not statistical significance. All outcomes concern workshop creations, with no delayed follow-up reported (p. 3, Section III.B; p. 8, Section IV.C).
